title: De Soto through the South-East to the Mississippi, 1539–43
summary: De Soto landed on the Gulf coast of Florida with some 600 men, 200 horses and a herd of pigs, and spent three years going north-east through the Apalachee and Cofitachequi country, west across the Appalachians and the Mississippi, and on into Arkansas. He was seeking gold and found none; he took people as porters and guides and left disease behind. He died on the Mississippi, and the survivors went down the river in boats and on to Pánuco. Moscoso's march west into Texas in 1542–43 is left off the map.

legs.doubt: The landing is put at Tampa Bay or Charlotte Harbor by different readers.

events.label: Anhaica: the first winter
events.text: The army wintered in the Apalachee town, which archaeologists found in 1987 at Tallahassee: the first confirmed site where the expedition stayed.

events.label: The Mississippi crossed
events.doubt: The crossing place is put at several points from southern Tennessee to Mississippi.
events.text: The first recorded European sight of the river's lower reaches. The men built barges; the Quapaw or their neighbours met them on the water.
